lede: Wagner Barja was sent by Funarte (Fundação Nacional de Arte) to Nossa Senhora de Cachoeira de Arari, in Pará.
about.0:
Wagner Barja was sent by Funarte (Fundação Nacional de Arte),
to Nossa Senhora de Cachoeira de Arari, in Pará. The town houses
the Museu do Marajó, founded in 1972 by the Italian priest Giovanni
Gallo, an important local leader, together with the population (in part remnants of quilombola communities). Around the museum of the
marajoara man and of his cultural cosmology, social life would be
structured. After the priest’s death, the community continued to grow squeezed between the large estates and the river, sharpening the conflicts between
local power (the landowners) and the community leaders.
The artist’s proposal then consisted in the carrying out, by everyone, of
a great performative act, a celebration occupying part
of those unproductive lands with the cultural universe of the
marajoara man: the boi-bumbá, the flag of the Divino, among others. On the day
of the event, Barja observed something unexpected: some 300 people in the streets, busy with their day-to-day affairs, held
a rolled-up piece of paper in their hand, a blank sheet. Men, women, children, marajoara prostitutes thus simulated the possession
of their plot of land. That is, they fictionalized the reversal of their own
precarious situation, they imagined and enacted the change in their
lives. With the feast of the ox, the feast of the occupation, they founded the Bairro
do Gallo. The municipal government took a supportive position, and they are still there.
The artist was there a catalyst of the dormant powers that
needed only a trigger in order to emerge. Fiction is not the
creation of an illusory world set against the real: it is unheard-of
and daring forms of connection between a referential world and
other worlds (including potential ones) that traverse or orbit
around it. Such is its cosmogonic power, its power of
imagination, freedom and creation. Art is not what takes upon itself the
task of fictionalizing for the other, it is what opens to the other the conditions and possibilities for him to operate his own creative fiction.
Fiction, phantasia for the Greeks, designated “the arts of forging”. They are
gestures of imagining and forging, gestures of a radical reinvention of
worlds. Marisa Flórido César, 2014

Marisa Flórido César

unproductive land.
